literal: Corrupt clerks in turn slandered and memorialized against him; he was cast into prison.
idiomatic: Corrupt clerks turned on him with false accusations; he was thrown into prison.

literal: Soon he was released, did not return home, and went straight to the office to handle affairs.
idiomatic: He was soon released, did not go home, and went straight to his office to work.

literal: At death he left instructions for a simple burial, no stele or tablet, and no request for a posthumous title.
idiomatic: When he died he ordered a plain burial—no stele, no marker, no posthumous title sought.

literal: Posthumously made Governor of Guazhou.
idiomatic: He was posthumously made Governor of Guazhou.

literal: In Wuping, because his son Shisu had long held confidential duties, he was again posthumously made Pillar of State, posthumous name Zhenhui.
idiomatic: In the Wuping era, because his son Shisu had long handled state secrets, he was again posthumously made Pillar of State with the posthumous name Upright and Gracious.

literal: Youdao was upright and rigid, hating evil as though it were a foe; seeing anyone commit a crime, he wished to bring them to the utmost penalty.
idiomatic: Youdao was rigidly upright and hated wrongdoing like an enemy; whenever he saw a crime he wanted the harshest penalty applied.

literal: He impeached matters before his eyes and also loved to probe private affairs.
idiomatic: He impeached whatever came before him and loved to probe private conduct as well.

literal: In questioning prisoners and examining circumstances, beating and flogging were severe and cruel.
idiomatic: In interrogation he read circumstances through beatings that were savage and cruel.

literal: Yanzhou Inspector Li Zizhen was greedy and violent in the province; Youdao investigated him.
idiomatic: Li Zizhen, inspector of Yanzhou, was greedy and brutal in his province; Youdao took up the case.

literal: Gao Cheng, because Zizhen had shared in the merit of founding the righteous cause, intended to be forbearing.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng meant to show forbearance because Zizhen had helped in the founding struggle.

literal: Youdao suspected Chen Yuankang was his inside helper and secretly reported: "Zizhen and Yuankang associate; I fear they have other private requests.
idiomatic: Youdao suspected Chen Yuankang was backing him from within and secretly wrote, "Zizhen and Yuankang are close; I fear there are other private arrangements.

literal: " Gao Cheng in anger, at the Masters of Writing main hall assembled the hundred officials and beat Zizhen to death.
idiomatic: " Gao Cheng flew into a rage, assembled the hundred officials in the main hall of the Masters of Writing, and beat Zizhen to death on the spot.

literal: Moreover, men of Yanzhou while he still lived built a shrine to Youdao, with his image inscribed "Lord Loyal and Pure."
idiomatic: Men of Yanzhou also built him a living shrine, with an image inscribed "Lord Loyal and Pure."

literal: Youdao separately impeached Ji Ning and four others to die together, with a look of pleasure.
idiomatic: Youdao separately impeached Ji Ning and four others for the same death sentence, his face bright with satisfaction.

literal: Court gentlemen greatly despised him for it.
idiomatic: Court gentlemen despised him for it.

literal: Yet he valued friendship and kept the bond of pledged word.
idiomatic: Yet he prized friendship and kept his pledged word.

literal: Through his offices he was stern and orderly, yet at times took large bribes and distributed them to kin and friends in hardship and want; for orphaned men and women he arranged marriages, and at funerals he was always mournful and personally assisted in the rites.
idiomatic: In office he was stern and exacting, yet he also took heavy bribes and shared them with kin and friends in need; he arranged marriages for orphaned men and women, and at every funeral he mourned deeply and handled the rites himself.

literal: As Si Province regulator he clashed with the princes governing Changlean and Xihe; when the two princes died, he showed care in every matter concerning them. With Dunqiu Li Jiang, after one meeting they swore death friendship.
idiomatic: As Si Province regulator he fell out with the Changlean and Xihe princes; when both died he still looked after their affairs. With Li Jiang of Dunqiu he met once and swore friendship unto death.

literal: Jiang said: "My years and rank are already high.
idiomatic: Jiang said, "My years and rank are already high.

literal: When the time comes I will employ my younger brother as aide; having him face north toward me is enough.
idiomatic: When the time comes I will use my younger brother as aide; let him face north to me and that will do.

literal: " Youdao said: "I cannot.
idiomatic: " Youdao said, "I cannot.

literal: " Before long Jiang became Intendant of Henan and summoned Youdao as impartial judge; messengers came in succession, and he received him with headcloth, hand in hand in merry banter.
idiomatic: " Soon Jiang became Intendant of Henan and appointed Youdao impartial judge; envoys came one after another, and he received him informally, clasping hands in easy jest.

literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Jiang accepted his commission and went out as envoy to Xuzhou; Area Commander Yuan Fu with the city man Zhao Shao killed him by force of arms.
idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Jiang accepted his orders and went to Xuzhou on mission; Area Commander Yuan Fu and a townsman named Zhao Shao killed him with troops.

literal: Youdao pleaded Jiang's grievance and cleared his name, and also memorialized to request posthumous honors, turning back one grade from his own examination to add to Jiang's.
idiomatic: Youdao sued to clear Jiang's name and won, then memorialized for posthumous honors, deducting one grade from his own review to add to Jiang's.

literal: He also befriended Liu Yin and entrusted Yin's younger brother Cui at Xuzhou to kill Zhao Shao.
idiomatic: He also befriended Liu Yin and had Yin's younger brother Cui kill Zhao Shao at Xuzhou.

literal: Later Liu Yin was executed by law at Luoyang; Cui rebelled at Xuzhou, government troops suppressed him, and Cui's head was exposed at Ye market.
idiomatic: Later Liu Yin was executed at Luoyang; Cui rebelled in Xuzhou, government troops put him down, and his head was displayed in the Ye market.

literal: Sun Teng sent a client to tell the market office that only after five million cash was received would they be allowed to take it down.
idiomatic: Sun Teng sent an agent to the market office saying they could collect the head only after five million cash was paid.

literal: Youdao was then Central Army aide of Si Province; he had his household pose as Liu Cui's kin, filed suit in the province, and by law obtained a ruling of "permitted" and memorialized it.
idiomatic: Youdao was then Central Army aide in Si Province; he had his household pose as Liu Cui's relatives, sue in the province, obtain a legal ruling of "permitted," and memorialized it.

literal: When the edict arrived, the market office still would not allow it.
idiomatic: When the edict arrived, the market office still refused.

literal: Youdao flogged the office staff and compelled them to hand it over at once.
idiomatic: Youdao beat the market staff and forced them to surrender the head immediately.

literal: When Teng heard of it he was greatly enraged.
idiomatic: Teng was furious when he heard.

literal: At the time Li Jiang's two sons Gou and Xun lived in poverty; Youdao later had them seek three rich men on capital charges, obtain acquittal, and in all got one million five hundred thousand cash, which he gave entirely to Gou and Xun.
idiomatic: Li Jiang's sons Gou and Xun were then poor; Youdao later had them find three wealthy men facing capital charges, win acquittals, and collect one million five hundred thousand cash, which he gave them in full.

literal: His bravado and chivalric partisanship were like this.
idiomatic: His swaggering, faction-bound chivalry was of this sort.

literal: People said at the time: "Youdao has a monkey's face, Lu Cao a tadpole's shape; awareness has nothing to do with looks—why say the ugly must be without feeling?
idiomatic: A saying of the time ran, "Youdao has a monkey's face and Lu Cao a tadpole's body—mind has nothing to do with looks; why assume the ugly are heartless?

literal: " Gou once at Youdao's reception for guests playfully said to him: "Your worthy cousin is outside the gate, a very fine man—you should go welcome him yourself.
idiomatic: " Once, while Gou was at Youdao's gathering of guests, he teased him: "Your excellent cousin is at the gate—a fine fellow; you ought to welcome him yourself.

literal: " He had him announced under the name "clansman cousin You Shan."
idiomatic: " He sent word in under the name "clansman You Shan."

literal: " Youdao went out to see him—it was monkey cap and clothes.
idiomatic: " Youdao went out to receive him and found monkey cap and clothes.

literal: He was about to break with Gou, but Gou apologized and they were suddenly as before.
idiomatic: He was ready to break with Gou, but Gou apologized and they were suddenly close again.

literal: After Youdao died, Gou became chief clerk of Dingzhou; Youdao's third son Shisun was Ink Office registrar and recorder for the Prince of Boling, and together with the registry keeper falsely memorialized against Gou.
idiomatic: After Youdao's death, Gou became chief clerk of Dingzhou; Youdao's third son Shisun, registrar in the Ink Office and recorder to the Prince of Boling, joined the registry keeper in a false accusation against Gou.

literal: Gou in the detention house offered sacrifice to Youdao and appealed to him.
idiomatic: Imprisoned, Gou sacrificed to Youdao and pleaded to him.

literal: Shixun by day lay asleep as in a dream and saw Youdao angrily addressing him: "Jiang and I had bond of grace and duty—do you not know it? How can you join petty men to plot against an upright man!
idiomatic: Shixun napped by day as if dreaming and saw Youdao rebuke him: "Jiang and I were bound in grace and duty—do you not know it? How dare you join petty men to trap an upright man!

literal: " Shixun in alarm knelt and said: "I dare not, I dare not.
idiomatic: " Shixun knelt in terror and said, "I dare not, I dare not.

literal: " Within ten days he died.
idiomatic: " Within ten days he was dead.

literal: Youdao often admonished his sons Shisu, Shiyue, Shishen, and others: "My law enforcement is too rigid; I have repeatedly met setbacks—such is my nature; descendants are not fit to take me as teacher.
idiomatic: Youdao often warned his sons Shisu, Shiyue, Shishen, and the rest: "I enforced the law too harshly and met setback after setback—that is my nature; my descendants should not take me as their model.

literal: " The sons obeyed their father's words and were gentle and modest.
idiomatic: " His sons obeyed and were gentle and humble.

literal: Shisu was deep, reticent, and few of words, with talent and judgment.
idiomatic: Shisu was reserved and sparing of speech, with talent and discernment.

literal: He was gradually promoted to Secretariat Attendant.
idiomatic: He rose gradually to Secretariat Attendant.

literal: Zhao Yanshen brought him into the inner secretariat to share confidential duties; he passed through Secretariat and Yellow Gate Attendant posts, was promoted to Pillar of State and Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, and regularly headed the Yellow Gate Attendant office.
idiomatic: Zhao Yanshen brought him into the inner secretariat for confidential work; he served as secretariat and yellow gate attendant, then was promoted to Pillar of State and scattered-cavalry regular attendant, usually heading the yellow gate attendant office.

literal: He held himself at the nerve center of power for nearly twenty years, circumspect, warm, and respectful, and was greatly valued by Yanshen.
idiomatic: For nearly twenty years he stood at the heart of power, careful, warm, and respectful, and Yanshen held him in high regard.

literal: At first Zu Ting controlled court affairs and sent Yanshen out as inspector.
idiomatic: At first Zu Ting ran the government and sent Yanshen out as provincial inspector.

literal: Ting memorialized to make Shisu Administrator of Dong commandery; Secretariat Attendant Li Delin told Ting to keep him, and thereby he was returned and made Yellow Gate Attendant, again sharing confidential duties.
idiomatic: Ting memorialized to make Shisu administrator of Dong commandery; secretariat attendant Li Delin urged Ting to keep him, so he was recalled and made yellow gate attendant, again in confidential work.

literal: Shiyue was also a good man, office Master of Writing Left Vice Director.
idiomatic: Shiyue was also a good man and served as left vice director of the masters of writing.

literal: Lu Fei, styled Zizhang, was a man of Zhuo in Fanyang.
idiomatic: Lu Fei, courtesy name Zizhang, came from Zhuo in Fanyang.

literal: His father Tong was Wei Palace Attendant Master of Writing.
idiomatic: His father Tong had been palace attendant master of writing under the Wei.

literal: Fei's nature was cruel; he was known for forceful judgment.
idiomatic: Fei was cruel by nature and famed for harsh, decisive rulings.

literal: Gao Cheng summoned him as legal-prison aide in the chancellor's office.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng brought him in as legal-prison aide in the chancellor's office.

literal: He said to him: "Reckless and terse, yet splendor to completion—not a fine name.
idiomatic: He told him, "'Reckless and terse, yet splendor to completion'—not a flattering name.

literal: " In Tianbao he was gradually promoted to Master of Writing Left Vice Director, separately in charge of metropolitan-area imperial prison cases, cruel and excessive beyond what human feeling allows.
idiomatic: " In the Tianbao era he rose to left vice director of the masters of writing and separately ran capital-region imperial prison cases with cruelty beyond ordinary humanity.

literal: Without regard to whether the matter was great or small, torture exceeded bounds; under the great rod and chariot wheel hub those who died were not one.
idiomatic: Regardless of the crime's scale, torture went too far; not a few died under the great rod or the chariot wheel.

literal: Sometimes in severe winter's cold he placed prisoners on ice and snow;
idiomatic: Sometimes in bitter midwinter he set prisoners on ice and snow;

literal: sometimes in midsummer's fierce heat he exposed them under the sun.
idiomatic: sometimes in blazing midsummer he left them in the open sun.

literal: Those wrongly framed and driven to death numbered in the hundreds before and after.
idiomatic: Those he framed to death numbered in the hundreds.

literal: He also watched officials' faults and at every move memorialized the throne; when court gentlemen saw him, none did not walk with shortened steps and held breath—all called him Investigator Lu.
idiomatic: He also spied on officials' faults and reported every move; court gentlemen shortened their steps and held their breath at the sight of him, and all called him Investigator Lu.

literal: Fei later for slandering the history, together with Li Shu, died of flogging-wounds in prison.
idiomatic: Fei later slandered the history; he and Li Shu both died in prison of flogging wounds.

literal: Bi Yiyun, childhood name Tuo'er.
idiomatic: Bi Yiyun's childhood name was Tuo'er.

literal: In youth he was rough and chivalric; his family was on Yanzhou's northern border and often robbed travelers—the province and district suffered from him.
idiomatic: Young, he was rough and swaggering; his family lived on Yanzhou's northern frontier and often robbed travelers, to the province's grief.

literal: Only late did he restrain himself and enter office.
idiomatic: Only late in life did he reform and take office.

literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Masters of Writing Director of the Bureau of Punishments.
idiomatic: He rose to director of the bureau of punishments in the masters of writing.

literal: His nature was severe and cruel, and in affairs he was largely capable and effective.
idiomatic: He was severe and cruel, but in business he was sharp and effective.

literal: When Gao Cheng was chancellor he found him fit for duty and ordered a universal investigation of false officials, using exclusively chariot-wheel torture; what was obtained was very great.
idiomatic: When Gao Cheng was chancellor he judged him capable and ordered a sweep for false officials, relying chiefly on chariot-wheel torture; the haul was enormous.

literal: Yet resentment and slander rose greatly.
idiomatic: Yet resentment and outcry rose everywhere.

literal: He was once sued by a Si Province clerk who said he had skimmed funds and altered documents together.
idiomatic: A Si Province clerk once sued him, claiming he had skimmed funds and falsified documents.

literal: Gao Cheng, because he was pressing false officials and the crowd was resentful, questioned nothing of it; instead he detained several clerks and beheaded them.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng, since Yiyun was exposing false officials and the crowd was bitter, ignored the charge and instead detained several clerks and beheaded them.

literal: From this his zeal for interrogation sharpened and his dread name grew daily.
idiomatic: After that his zeal for interrogation sharpened and his fearsome name spread.

literal: When Gao Yang received the abdication he was made Attending Censor for Drafting; in impeachment he did not avoid meritorious kin.
idiomatic: When Gao Yang took the throne he was made attending censor for drafting and in impeachment spared no meritorious kin.

literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Censor-in-Chief; restraints and impeachment grew still sharper.
idiomatic: He rose to censor-in-chief, and his restraints and impeachments grew still harsher.

literal: Yet he was overbearing and unfair and was repeatedly sued in resentment.
idiomatic: Yet he was domineering and unjust and was sued again and again out of spite.

literal: Formerly as Administrator of Ji Commandery, Zhai Song memorialized listing: "Yi Yun's paternal cousin Sengming owed official debt; having first served as metropolitan-area chief clerk, he did not accept Yi Yun's subordinates and set strict deadlines for collection; thereby nursing a grudge, he repeatedly sent censors through the commandery to investigate, wishing to impeach each other.
idiomatic: Earlier, as administrator of Ji commandery, Zhai Song had memorialized: "Yiyun's cousin Sengming owed official debt; when Sengming was metropolitan chief clerk he refused Yiyun's men and set harsh collection deadlines; nursing a grudge, Yiyun kept sending censors through the commandery to investigate and impeach him.

literal: He was also charged with privately hoarding artisans; his household had more than ten looms weaving brocade, and moreover made gold and silver vessels.
idiomatic: He was also charged with hiding artisans privately—more than ten brocade looms at home and gold and silver work besides.

literal: " He was then detained.
idiomatic: " He was then placed under detention.

literal: Soon he was released and made Left Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Works.
idiomatic: He was soon released and made left chief clerk of the ministry of works.

literal: Master of Writing Left Vice Director Sima Zirui memorialized to impeach Yi Yun, stating: "In the fourth month of the first year of Tianbao, on the day of the Empress Dowager Dou's imperial aunt's burial, inner and outer officials of every rank went to her residence to mourn; Yi Yun only sent a censor to submit his name and himself did not go.
idiomatic: Left vice director Sima Zirui impeached Yiyun, writing: "In the fourth month of Tianbao year one, on the burial day of Empress Dowager Dou's imperial aunt, officials inside and out went to mourn; Yiyun only sent a censor to register his name and did not attend.

literal: Moreover Yi Yun reported: 'My wife died and I am poor and alone; I later took Li Shi'an's daughter as wife.
idiomatic: Yiyun had also reported, 'My wife died and I am poor and alone; I later took Li Shi'an's daughter in marriage.

literal: Though Shi'an's person is still within mourning for his father, his daughter for her grandfather had already passed the peaceful day; I specially beg a secret welcome and dare not prepare full rites.'
idiomatic: Though Shi'an is still in mourning for his father, his daughter had already passed the grandfather's peaceful day; I beg a secret welcome and dare not hold full ceremony.'

literal: Yet on the night Yi Yun's marriage was completed, the crowd was fully stored and set out; on the fixed day he bowed at the gate, outriders cleared the road, feathered insignia were arrayed in splendor, and moreover twenty bureau clerks were dispatched to demand fresh clothes and attend behind his carriage.
idiomatic: Yet on his wedding night the stores were piled high; on the appointed day he bowed at the gate, runners cleared the road, feathered guards paraded in splendor, and twenty bureau clerks were sent to demand fresh dress and follow his carriage.

literal: It was plainly a shameless demand for marriage and deception importuning superiors.
idiomatic: It was plainly a shameless rush to marry and a lie pressed on his superiors.

literal: Yi Yun's assets and dwellings were enough to be called grand and extreme; suddenly to speak of poverty and solitude was also pretense and fraud.
idiomatic: Yiyun's property and house were lavish enough to count as grand; to call himself poor and alone was fraud as well.

literal: When judges are like this, where can upright rule be entrusted?
idiomatic: If judges behave thus, where is upright law to be found?

literal: Moreover when the emperor visited Jinyang, the chief seat ruled: 'For bowing the salutation memorial, those of fifth rank and above from fourth rank down are to go the day before to the southern capital office to sign the memorial; those of third rank and above sign it on the day itself.'
idiomatic: When the emperor went to Jinyang, the chief seat ruled: 'For the bowing-salutation memorial, officials from fourth rank down through fifth rank and up must sign at the southern capital office the day before; third rank and above sign on the day itself.'

literal: Yi Yun then violated precedent; on the day of signing the memorial he demanded the memorial and signed it first at home, and on the day itself then claimed private taboo and did not come.
idiomatic: Yiyun broke precedent: on signing day he had the memorial brought home and signed first, then on the day itself pleaded private taboo and stayed away.

literal: " Thereupon an edict handed him to the Court of Judicature for sentencing; soon an order excused further prosecution.
idiomatic: " An edict sent him to the Court of Judicature; soon another order halted the case.

literal: Zirui again memorialized to impeach Yi Yun on more than ten matters, mostly trivial; the crime stopped at a fine and did not reach removal.
idiomatic: Zirui impeached him again on more than ten petty counts; punishment stopped at a fine and did not cost him his post.

literal: Zirui's cousin Xiaonan was Inspector of North Yuzhou; Yi Yun sent Censor Zhang Zijie to the province to gather hearsay and first detained his registry keeper, household clients, and the like.
idiomatic: Zirui's cousin Xiaonan was inspector of North Yuzhou; Yiyun sent censor Zhang Zijie to gather rumors and first detained his registry keeper, household agents, and the like.

literal: Xiaonan in peril and fear then rebelled and entered Zhou.
idiomatic: Terrified, Xiaonan rebelled and fled to Zhou.

literal: Opinion of the time laid blame on Yi Yun, saying he had plotted retaliation against Zirui; the matter also reached the throne.
idiomatic: Public opinion blamed Yiyun for scheming revenge on Zirui, and word reached the throne.

literal: Before this at banquets and feasts Yi Yun was always present; from this time onward his appearances at gatherings grew somewhat sparse and his reputation greatly fell.
idiomatic: Before this he had always been at court feasts; afterward he was seen less often and his standing collapsed.

literal: At the beginning of Qianming, Zirui was transferred to Censor-in-Chief.
idiomatic: Early in Qianming, Zirui became censor-in-chief.

literal: Zheng Zimo was then in active use; Yi Yun's paternal aunt was Zimo's grandmother, and he was therefore made Minister of Revenue and acting Left Vice Director.
idiomatic: Zheng Zimo was then in favor; Yiyun's aunt was Zimo's grandmother, so he was made minister of revenue and acting left vice director.

literal: After Zimo was executed, the left vice director post was at once relinquished.
idiomatic: After Zimo was killed, he gave up the acting left vice director post at once.

literal: When Gao Yan went to Jinyang, Gao Yuanhai remained at Ye; Yi Yun clung to him in deep dependence.
idiomatic: When Gao Yan went to Jinyang and Gao Yuanhai stayed at Ye, Yiyun attached himself to Yuanhai with deep reliance.
